title: 2 Thessalonians 3:1–5
context: Paul asks for prayer for the gospel’s advance and protection from opposition, then turns to the Lord’s faithfulness toward the church. Confidence in divine help accompanies commands to obey and prayer for love and perseverance. Both traditions affirm sustaining grace; they differ in how this assurance relates to the possibility of finally abandoning faith.

verses.text: Finally, brothers, pray for us, that the word of the Lord may spread rapidly and be glorified, even as also with you,
verses.arminianNotes: Paul asks the church to pray for the gospel’s advance. Arminian readers see prayer and proclamation as meaningful participation in God’s gracious mission, as the Thessalonians’ own reception illustrates.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers see prayer and preaching as means God appoints for spreading his word. Confidence in his purpose does not make missionary prayer unnecessary.

verses.text: and that we may be delivered from unreasonable and evil men; for not all have faith.
verses.arminianNotes: Paul asks for rescue from hostile people and acknowledges that not everyone believes. Arminian readers recognize that the gospel can be resisted without treating opponents as beyond the reach of grace.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers likewise acknowledge real unbelief and seek protection for gospel workers. This observation alone does not spell out the full doctrine of election or identify who may yet come to faith.

verses.text: But the Lord is faithful, who will establish you and guard you from the evil one.
verses.arminianNotes: The Lord’s faithfulness supports believers against evil. Arminian readers affirm reliable sustaining grace while reading this assurance alongside the calls to continuing faith and obedience, not as permission to abandon Christ.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers see the Lord’s faithfulness as grounding the preservation of his people. He establishes and guards them so that they persevere, without promising freedom from all suffering or temptation.
verses.keyContrast: Both rest in the Lord’s faithful protection. Arminian readers affirm sustaining grace without treating final perseverance as unconditional; Reformed readers understand God’s preservation as securing the enduring faith of the truly regenerate.

verses.text: We have confidence in the Lord concerning you, that you both do and will do the things we command.
verses.arminianNotes: Paul’s confidence is in the Lord as the church obeys. Arminian readers see gracious help sustaining responsible action rather than obedience arising independently of God.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers emphasize that confidence in God gives Paul confidence in the church’s continuing obedience. Both affirm that trust in divine help and practical exhortation belong together.

verses.text: May the Lord direct your hearts into God’s love and into the perseverance of Christ.
verses.arminianNotes: Paul prays for hearts directed into God’s love and Christ’s perseverance. Arminian readers seek divine help for patient endurance rather than relying on determination alone.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers likewise see the Lord shaping the heart’s loves and endurance. The prayer calls the church into Christlike steadfastness amid pressures and delays.
